chunks: Indeed, God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant except that He has made incumbent upon him, regarding it, the Proof from God.
So whoever God has favoured by making him strong, his obligation upon him is to fulfill what He has charged him with and to bear [the burden of] those who are below him among those weaker than him.
And whoever God has favoured by making him prosperous, his obligation upon him is his wealth, then his covenant of commitment toward the poor afterwards through his voluntary charitable acts.

And whoever God has favoured by making him noble in his household and beautiful in his appearance, his obligation upon him is that he praise God the Exalted for that, and that he not be arrogant toward others so that he withholds the rights of the weak because of his noble state and beauty.

key_terms.احْتِمَالُ: Bearing/tolerating — referring to the strong person's duty to patiently support and carry the burden of the weak
key_terms.الْحُجَّةَ: The Proof/obligation — in this context a divinely-established responsibility that each person is accountable for, not merely an argument
key_terms.مُوَسَّعاً: Prosperous/capacious — one who has been given financial abundance
key_terms.نَوَافِلِهِ: His voluntary deeds — supererogatory acts of charity beyond the obligatory minimum

ai.seo_question: What obligation does Islam place on the strong, wealthy, and noble according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that every divine blessing carries with it a corresponding obligation (hujja). The strong must fulfill their duties and support the weak; the wealthy must spend their wealth and maintain commitment to the poor through voluntary charity; the nobly born and beautiful must thank God and refrain from arrogance that would lead to denying the rights of the disadvantaged. The teaching reflects the Shia theological principle that divine bounties are tests (ibtila') and that accountability before God is proportional to the gifts one receives.
word_analysis: He has made incumbent upon him
